subject: Draft: measurement plan for the team lead feedback programme
mail: Hi! Here's my draft measurement plan for the feedback conversations programme for team leads at the distribution centre. Could you check it before it goes to the site director?
snippets: Programme: monthly one-to-ones and feedback skills for 22 team leads.
Goal: lower short-term absence and turnover.
The site has a works council and a DPO.
draft_title: Measurement plan: feedback conversations for team leads
draft: Baseline: short-term absence and voluntary turnover per team over the last 12 months, from HR.
Behaviour: team leads hold a monthly one-to-one with each team member, logged in the HR system.
Every quarter, a sample of team members answers three questions on whether their team lead gives them useful feedback.
Business metric: short-term absence and turnover in teams whose lead has been through the programme, compared with teams still waiting.
To keep it sharp, we rank team leads individually on their team's absence and share the ranking in the monthly management meeting.
Collection: monthly HR export and the quarterly pulse, reviewed after six months.
flaw_why: Ranking named team leads on their team's absence turns the measurement into a blame tool, is unreliable for small teams, and uses employee data in a way the works council and DPO would need to approve.
fix: Compare groups (trained versus waiting) instead of individuals, and agree the use of the data with the works council and DPO before starting.
debrief: Most of this plan is solid: a baseline, a behaviour, a comparison group. The ranking line is the kind of 'sharpening' that kills trust and, in Belgium, starts a works council discussion. Group comparisons answer the same question without naming anyone.
